name: Possible DVT or pulmonary embolism
action: Stop physiotherapy. Refer to A&E now for DVT or PE assessment (Doppler, Wells score, D-dimer; CT pulmonary angiography for PE).
source: Framework §11 (DVT and PE) and §14 (immediate emergency: DVT / PE symptoms)

name: Possible cauda equina syndrome
action: Stop physiotherapy. Refer to A&E now for emergency MRI; do not discharge or delay.
source: Framework §4A (cauda equina: bladder or bowel dysfunction, saddle anaesthesia) and §14

name: Possible septic arthritis
action: Stop physiotherapy. Refer to A&E now for joint aspiration.
source: Framework §3 (fever with musculoskeletal pain), §6, §9 and §14 (septic arthritis suspicion)

name: Fever with musculoskeletal pain
action: Possible septic arthritis or infection: emergency referral before any physiotherapy.
source: Framework §3 (fever + MSK pain: emergency referral)

name: Possible cauda equina syndrome (back)
action: Stop physiotherapy. Refer to A&E now for emergency MRI; neurosurgical review within hours.
source: Framework §4A (NICE CKS revised criteria) and §4D

name: Possible cervical arterial dysfunction
action: Defer all manual therapy. Same-day medical referral (vascular or neurological) under the IFOMPT cervical framework.
source: Framework §4B (5Ds and 3Ns, IFOMPT 2023) and §14 (cervical arterial dysfunction)

name: Possible cervical myelopathy
action: Urgent neurological referral and MRI before treatment.
source: Framework §4B (bilateral arm symptoms with gait disturbance)

name: History of cancer with new pain
action: Treat new pain as possible metastasis until cleared: same-day oncology referral before physiotherapy.
source: Framework §3, §13 (history of cancer + new or changing pain) and §19 (cancer survivors)

name: Unexplained weight loss over the threshold
action: Possible malignancy: urgent physician referral.
source: Framework §3 and §13 (unexplained weight loss over 5 kg in 6 months); decision #5

name: Unexplained weight loss
action: Ask about the amount and period; re-screen for malignancy features at each visit.
source: Framework §1 and §3

name: Malignancy risk cluster
action: Urgent imaging before loading treatment (multi red flag cluster).
source: Framework §3 and §13 (age over 50 with a risk factor: urgent imaging)

name: Severe or non-mechanical night pain
action: Possible tumour or infection: medical referral and imaging work-up.
source: Framework §3 (night pain unrelieved by rest) and §14 (severe unexplained night pain)

name: Progressive neurological weakness
action: Same-day specialist review; full neurological examination before treatment.
source: Framework §14 (rapid progressive weakness)

name: Rapidly worsening symptoms
action: Stop routine rehabilitation and refer for medical review.
source: Framework §20 (severe, progressive or deteriorating: stop and refer)

name: Dizziness, blackouts or balance problems
action: Medical review before treatment; for neck presentations apply the cervical vascular screen.
source: Framework §1 and §4B

name: Severe fatigue or unexplained weakness
action: Rheumatology, haematology or oncology screening with bloods.
source: Framework §3 (severe fatigue + inflammatory pattern) and §13 (unexplained fatigue)

name: Prolonged morning stiffness
action: Possible inflammatory arthritis: rheumatology referral with ESR, CRP, RF and anti-CCP.
source: Framework §12 (morning stiffness over 60 minutes); decision #6

name: Immunocompromised, diabetic or on long-term steroids
action: Lower referral threshold and re-screen more often (infection and fracture risk).
source: Framework §19 (high-risk populations)

name: Recent infection, surgery or hospitalisation
action: DVT and infection vigilance: Wells score and vascular check at every assessment.
source: Framework §11 and §19 (post-surgical patients)

name: Recent trauma or accident
action: Screen for fracture before loading (Ottawa rules where they apply).
source: Framework §1, §9, §10 and §16
